Yalda Night Ajeel (Mixed Nuts and Dried Fruits)

Served at: Yalda Night

Serves 8-10Prep 15 minCook 10 min (optional toasting)

Yalda Night, or Shab-e Yalda, marks the winter solstice and the longest night of the year, a cherished ancient Persian celebration of light overcoming darkness. Ajeel, a vibrant mix of nuts and dried fruits, is a cornerstone of the Yalda spread, symbolizing abundance, health, and the bounty of the harvest, enjoyed by families gathered together to read poetry and share stories.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (120 g) walnuts, shelled
  • 1 cup (120 g) almonds, raw or lightly roasted
  • 1 cup (120 g) pistachios, shelled
  • 1/2 cup (60 g) hazelnuts, raw or lightly roasted
  • 1/2 cup (60 g) cashews, raw or lightly roasted
  • 1/2 cup (80 g) golden raisins
  • 1/2 cup (80 g) dark raisins
  • 1/2 cup (75 g) dried mulberries
  • 1/2 cup (75 g) dried figs, quartered or halved
  • 1/2 cup (75 g) dried apricots, halved
  • 1/4 cup (30 g) pumpkin seeds
  • 1/4 cup (30 g) sunflower seeds
  • 1/4 teaspoon sea salt (optional)

Method

  1. Preheat your oven to 300°F (150°C) if you wish to lightly toast the raw nuts and seeds. Skip this step if using pre-roasted nuts.
  2. Spread raw walnuts, almonds, hazelnuts, cashews, pumpkin seeds, and sunflower seeds in a single layer on a baking sheet.
  3. Toast in the preheated oven for 8-10 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until fragrant and lightly golden. Be careful not to burn them.
  4. Remove from the oven and let the toasted nuts and seeds cool completely on the baking sheet.
  5. In a large decorative bowl, combine the cooled toasted nuts and seeds with the pistachios, golden raisins, dark raisins, dried mulberries, dried figs, and dried apricots.
  6. If desired, sprinkle with a pinch of sea salt for enhanced flavor.
  7. Gently toss all the ingredients together until well combined.
  8. Arrange the ajeel attractively in serving bowls, often alongside fresh pomegranates and watermelon, for your Yalda Night celebration.

Tips

  • For the best flavor, use high-quality, fresh nuts and dried fruits. Avoid anything that smells stale or rancid.
  • Customize your ajeel by adding other favorites like dried cranberries, dates, or even roasted chickpeas (nokhodchi).
  • Store any leftover ajeel in an airtight container at room temperature for up to two weeks, or in the refrigerator for longer freshness.
